summary: Sound rewrite stage: the bisect cases separate the variables that case 2 confounded, so one check names the faulty variable whether or not the fix lands. However, the four fixes the change lists, (a) to (d), are already implemented in the stage-3 kernel, so the bisect output, not a blind rewrite of the loop, has to drive the fix.
justification: Diagnosis: case 2 (B=6, kv 0.25, grid 3, ~81 tiles per CTA) failed at rel L2 1.23, finite, with both combines. Case 1 (grid=device, at most 1 tile per CTA) passed. That places the bug in the main kernel and in something that only happens when a CTA runs several tiles or crosses requests. The harvest supports this, and the bisect plan is the right one: kv 0.25 alone; multi-tile with B=1 at 2/4/17 tiles, so no request crossing and the 17-tile case covers IDX_TILES rotation; plus the original case. WEAKEST LINK: I read splitkv_verify_wgmma_kernel on the s3 branch and the suspects (a) to (d) are already coded as the spec asks. m/l/oacc reset only at segment start (n==0 || lt==0). oacc is rescaled after wg_wait0 of the previous PV, i.e. before the next PV is issued. The full parity is (n/STAGES)&1 and the empty-wait parity ((n-1)/STAGES)&1 is correct for the refill slot. V^T uses buffer n&1 per tile. The FA3 Max_offset (P = 2^(s - (u - 8))) is present, with l and O both carrying the 2^8. k_scale is folded into the per-tile score scale and v_scale is applied in the merge. So the 'most likely cause' named in step (2) is probably not the cause. What I could not rule out by reading: (i) the bounded-wait abort, where flag_s[0] makes every later wait return at once and produces finite garbage of exactly this kind (rel L2 ~1); stage 3 never printed the error word; (ii) the page-index prefetch and request crossing inside a 16-tile meta block (issue_meta uses req_of per tile, which looks right); (iii) start_of/req_of/slot = bx + cb bookkeeping when a CTA spans several requests (the slot mapping is collision-free by my reading); (iv) kv_scale 0.25 with grid=device, which was never run. The milestones are physically plausible. verify is MMA-heavy (64 query rows per kv head = one m64 wgmma), wgmma is the right tensor-core path where mma.sync lost 1.7x (LESSONS 155), and the 2.4 TB/s target is ~1.7x stage 2's 1.44 TB/s. The expected direction (full verify_16/32 faster, everything else flat) matches the gate.
confounders: full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv / sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv (master): the s3 TU shares the pre-attention Triton kernel and the B8 combine lineage with the decode split-KV path. A passing self-check only clears the verify kernel. Any decode-row move in this check is master drift (full verify_1 and sliding verify_1 drifted +2-6% in the 03:41Z batch).

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup (master): the incumbent being replaced is paired FA3 main + combine + norm-gate. M2 must compare the wgmma kernel against those three rows in the same check, not against the headline.

full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (land candidate, not on master): untouched by this stage, but if it lands first the verify TU must be rebased (both add load_inline modules to the same file). No measurement confound.
interference: No companion. This is a rewrite stage whose deliverable is a named cause (M1) and, if the self-check passes, the kernel's own profile rows against FA3 (M2). The B=1 multi-tile cases and the split of case 2 are the in-run controls. A separate ab-revert run would add nothing that the per-case prints cannot. The next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: FP8 E4M3 P with Max_offset matches FA3's own FP8 path; the precision is fine as long as the coherent long-context self-check case passes (LESSONS 2026-10-25 FP8-P entry). Keep that case in the gate.
The bounded mbarrier wait must never trap or spin forever. The current abort flag is fine; keep it, and print the error word per case.
No other rules concerns: no process spawn (in-process load_inline), no work outside the timed call beyond prepare-time self-checks, all keys attended.
open_questions: Did case 2 trip the bounded-wait abort (error word 2)? Finite garbage at rel L2 ~1 is exactly what the abort path produces. If so, the bug is a real barrier deadlock or a too-small WAIT_LIMIT at 81 tiles per CTA, not softmax state.

BUILDER: make the bisect name the failing segment, not just the failing case. For the failing case, copy the per-slot partials (ws_acc O, ws_ml m/l) to host and compare each slot against a torch fp32 reference of that exact (CTA range, request) segment. Print the first bad slot with its CTA, request, tile count, whether it follows a request crossing, and whether its tile index is past 16. Also print the per-case error word. This turns one check into a line-level diagnosis even if no (2) fix lands.

BUILDER: do not rewrite items (a) to (d) blindly. They read correct on the s3 branch (reset at lt==0, rescale after wg_wait0, Max_offset, parity). Change the loop only where the bisect points, and keep any speculative edit behind a constexpr so the s3 path can be A/B'd inside the self-check.

When the self-check passes, choose wgmma regardless of the prepare timing (print both). This is a check, and M2 needs the kernel's profile rows. A timing hard gate would hide it, and prepare under-reads the judge by 20-25%.
